methods.label: Unroll the lampshade
methods.sourceMethod: 2023_AMC_12B_Q21: LIVE worked explanation and AoPS Wiki solution, using cone development and a tangent followed by an inner arc; the radial-projection lower bound supplies the shortest-path justification.

annotationRationale: The central ideas are developing the cone and finding a shortest path around the missing inner disk. The lower-bound argument also covers paths that wind around the lampshade. Both supplied references use the same geometric route, so they are combined into one complete method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independent calculation gives \(6\sqrt3+\pi\), choice E. The farthest top-rim point is diametrically opposite the bug. The statement, choices and key agree; no figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: LIVE and the AoPS solution attributed to Steven Chen use the same cone-development and tangent-plus-arc route, appropriately merged into one method. The candidate adds a complete lower bound covering winding paths. No shared-bank methods were supplied, and another route is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Cone development and circular-obstacle minimization are appropriate assessed concepts. Similarity, right-triangle geometry, tangents, arc length and the cosine-law comparison are appropriate support concepts.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The slant width is 6, giving developed rim radii 6 and 12 and endpoint angular separation \(\pi/2\). Tangency gives length \(6\sqrt3\) and leaves an inner arc of length \(\pi\). The radial-projection inequality is correct. Choosing a crossing at continuous angle \(\pi/3\) yields prefix length at least the tangent length and remaining length at least \(\pi\), including for winding routes. The constructed path attains both bounds and stays within the developed lampshade.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited references support the geometric construction. The candidate honestly uses source-informed-original status for nonofficial LIVE and AoPS material. Its expanded projection and winding argument is independently explained, and the prose does not reproduce the supplied explanations sentence by sentence.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why unfolding helps and why a straight segment is obstructed. The unfamiliar projection fact is justified using elementary distance comparisons and path subdivisions, without calculus. The angle tracking makes the global shortest-path claim reconstructible without a new diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All listed IDs have supplied definitions and are directly relevant. cnm_258 explicitly includes cone-development correspondence despite its area-oriented title. The obstacle synthesis node captures the essential minimization argument, while the remaining nodes supply its elementary components.
